column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1 on SDK 20.5.17, update 1.0.1; 73,512 shaders, all translated. Its shader libraries are in the IoStore container, Oodle-compressed shader groups that the port
# decodes with the game's own Oodle on the device (porter device_ue: one round, 5,919 groups, 74,244 shaders in 44 s), so the port needs the device connected.
# Tested 2026-11-06 on the Legion Y700 (TB322FC, Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, Android 16), docked (1920x1080): the brightness setting, the title, a new game (difficulty), the
# opening cinematic, the first road (walking, tutorials), the cutscene, the first battle's command menu; an autosave, and Continue from it after a restart.
# 60 fps (the profile's fps_target): frame work p50 about 16.5 ms, GPU 10-13 ms in the field and the cinematic, 0-6 dropped frames per 300; 0 audio underruns; no red line.
# Its sprite particles' parameters (R32F buffer textures of 36-44 elements at offsets not a multiple of Adreno's 64) are read from an aligned copy (gfx_vk_tex.c vk_tbuf_view).
# Its particle compute shaders write R32UI / R32I buffer textures through float images: those get an integer variant (gfx_vk_shader.c spv_int_images), and the battle's
# haze and dust sprites (vertex shader fb570ef861debd17) draw since.
# Open: the fires in the first battle's background (the battle tutorial's picture shows them) are not drawn: the game issues no draw for them. Every blended draw of the
# frame is in pass 22 (DM_VK_TRACE_PASS for passes 0-52), and DM_VK_X_FLAT_VS (in env.txt: pipelines made before it keep their state) shows what each is: fb570ef8 the
# haze sprites, 1300ca45ddca3566 (12 draws) and c55d54c8f41b1520 (4 draws) large flat ground-fog volumes, 70eb4102 the moon's glow. The fire light is there (orange on
# the wreck at the right in pass 22's input) and a 255x5 RGBA16F curve texture of fire colours is bound, but no flame geometry. Unreal culls GPU particle systems on the
# CPU from data it reads back: each frame the simulation copies its 32 KB count buffer (pool region 0x...630100 in the traces) to a ring of readback buffers, and those
# read as all zeros on the CPU in a memdump (the pools are zero-copy and measured coherent; the region is reused several times a frame, so not proven). Next: when the
# game reads those buffers (its fence / query wait against our completion), and what it reads, for the fire emitters.
